displayName: FCM stale-token cleanup spike (>100 per hour)

documentation.content:
The notify-* callables cleaned more than 100 stale FCM tokens in an hour (p99 of the `cleanedTokenCount` log field, M37). Potential incident (Slack #familyhq-ops), not a page.

Mass token invalidation usually means an external dependency changed:
- The Firebase project's FCM key was rotated.
- APNs revoked our certificate.
- The app shipped a major version that all clients re-registered through.

Prerequisite: this policy queries the user-defined log-based metric `logging.googleapis.com/user/notify_callable_cleaned_token_count` (DISTRIBUTION) - it must exist in the project first; see docs/runbooks/observability.md section 4 for the create command.

The aligner is ALIGN_PERCENTILE_99. GCP rejects DISTRIBUTION->scalar comparisons unless the aligner explicitly collapses the distribution: 'a time series of type DISTRIBUTION cannot be compared directly to a literal numeric threshold without first converting to a scalar via an explicit aligner such as ALIGN_PERCENTILE_50/95/99'. ALIGN_SUM was rejected at create time (verified 2026-06-16 against gcloud alpha monitoring policies create). Using p99 catches a single big spike, which is what we want operationally - if any cleanup event in the hour cleaned more than 100 tokens, the alert fires.

Runbook: docs/runbooks/observability.md (section 1, series 3).
